'''Azriel Lévy'''<ref>More commonly written with an accent in English sources, e.g., A. Lévy: ''A hierarchy of formulas in set theory'', [[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]], '''57''', 1965.</ref> ({{Langx|he|עזריאל לוי}}; born c. 1934) is an Israeli [[mathematician]], [[logician]], and a [[professor emeritus]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].

==Biography==
Lévy obtained his Ph.D. at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 1958, under the supervision of [[Abraham Fraenkel]] and [[Abraham Robinson]].  Later, using [[Paul Cohen (mathematician)|Cohen]]'s method of [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]], he proved several results on the [[Equiconsistency|consistency]] of various statements contradicting the [[axiom of choice]]. For example, with [[Joseph Halpern|J. D. Halpern]] he proved that the [[Boolean prime ideal theorem]] does not imply the axiom of choice. He discovered the models ''L''[''x''] used in [[inner model theory]].  He also introduced the notions of [[Lévy hierarchy]] of the formulas of [[set theory]], [[list of forcing notions#Levy collapsing|Levy collapse]] and the [[Feferman–Levy model]].

His students include [[Dov Gabbay]], [[Moti Gitik]], and [[Menachem Magidor]].
